brief: A small-parts organizer with at least six separate bins.

requirements.requirement: At least six separate bins for small parts
requirements.evidence: There are 6 bins, one in each of the 6 cells: 3 hex-bin-full-div2 and 3 hex-bin-half-div3, giving 15 compartments.

requirements.requirement: Works as a small-parts organizer, holding small parts
requirements.evidence: 11 piles of M3 screws, nuts and standoffs (prop:1 to prop:11) sit in the compartments, and all can be seen from above. The other 4 compartments are empty.
30 parts in a single-storey cluster of 6 cells, with end caps on the open faces and bolted joints.

finish.summary:
I built a compact organizer from six hex cells with a bin in each one, so it has six separate bins. The middle row (cells -1,0 / 0,0 / 1,0) has full-depth bins split into 2 compartments each. The other three cells (0,-1 / 0,1 / 1,-1) have half-depth bins split into 3 compartments each. That gives 15 compartments in all. Every open outer face is closed with an end cap, and the joints between cells are bolted. The total is 30 parts.

To show what it's for, I put piles of M3 screws, nuts and standoffs in 11 compartments; all 11 can be seen in the view from above. The configurator flags these piles as sitting below the bin rims, which is normal for parts lying loose in a bin. In the 2-compartment bins, 4 of the 6 compartments refused the pile I tried because it hit the bin wall. I left those 4 compartments empty. The build check passed with no issues, and the collision check came back clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
